$comment: Declares the builtin charset tables generated for the luit fork from ICU (uconv), or from iconv-lite ("iconv_lite") for encodings ICU has no converter for. The ICU version is pinned in the devcontainer/CI, iconv-lite's by package-lock.json, so the generated tables are reproducible.

tables.name: jisx0208-2007-0
tables.comment: The G1 (2-byte GR) plane of WHATWG/ICU euc-jp-2007. A superset table including JIS X 0208 + NEC special characters + IBM extensions. Referenced by charset.c's "JIS X 0208 (2007)" (T_9494).

overrides.comment: Wave dash position (EUC A1C1). Uses U+301C for decoding instead of WHATWG's default U+FF5E. The base row (U+FF5E) remains for encoding, so both are accepted (an asymmetric mapping).

tables.name: jisx0212.1990-0
tables.comment: Standard JIS X 0212 (via SS3). Shared between glibc EUC-JP-MS and ICU euc-jp-2007, so it can be reused for future variants too. Overrides charset.c's "JIS X 0212" (the existing xlfd name jisx0212.1990-0).

tables.name: cp932-direct-0
tables.comment: The default CP932 (Windows-31J) variant. SJIS->JIS's coordinate conversion formula can't handle the IBM extension range (0xFA-0xFC, etc.), so this is a direct raw-byte lookup instead (other_ja.c).

overrides.comment: Wave dash position (SJIS 0x8160). Same policy as the EUC-JP side.

tables.name: gb18030-2byte-0
tables.comment: GB18030's 2-byte part (the GBK-compatible range). A direct raw-byte lookup. Same approach as CP932 (other_ja.c).

tables.name: cp852-direct-0
tables.comment: CP852 (Central European DOS). stock luit's xlfd "ibm-cp852" had no data and was unmapped (confirmed by measurement).

tables.name: cp857-direct-0
tables.comment: CP857 (Turkish DOS). Newly added for the same reason as CP852.

tables.name: cp1125-direct-0
tables.comment: CP1125 (Ukrainian DOS). stock luit had no corresponding table and was unmapped.

tables.name: macroman-direct-0
tables.comment: Mac Roman. stock luit didn't recognize the -encoding name and silently fell back to ISO8859-1 (confirmed by measurement: Warning couldn't find charset data).

tables.name: koi8t-direct-0
tables.comment: KOI8-T (Tajik). ICU has no converter for it, so this one table comes from iconv-lite (pinned by package-lock.json), the library VS Code decodes files with; it must match Python's koi8_t and glibc's KOI8-T byte for byte (compared only, glibc's data isn't embedded).

tables.name: gbk-0
tables.comment: GBK. The xlfd name looked up by other.c's mapping_gbk(). The raw byte pair is used directly as source (an OTHER charset, no notion of shift). stock luit had no xlfd data and was unmapped (confirmed by measurement under musl).

tables.name: big5hkscs-0
tables.comment: Big5-HKSCS. The xlfd name looked up by other.c's init_hkscs(). Like GBK, an OTHER charset with the raw byte pair as source.

tables.name: big5.eten-0
tables.comment: Big5. Confirmed by measurement that charset.c's T_94192 (shift=0x8000) has n+shift matching the raw byte pair.

tables.name: gb2312.1980-0
tables.comment: GB2312. charset.c's T_9494 (shift=0) uses the GL scheme (high bit stripped), same as Japanese's jisx0208-2007-0. Confirmed by measurement (the raw-byte-pair approach mis-converted).

tables.name: ksc5601.1987-0
tables.comment: EUC-KR. Uses the GL scheme (T_9494, shift=0), same as GB2312.

tables.name: ibm-cp865
tables.comment: CP865 (Nordic DOS). Same reason and approach as CP852/857/1125. Reuses the existing "CP 865" charset row's xlfd as-is (no change needed to charset.c, just adding the table).

gb18030_4byte_ranges.comment: Extracts the BMP gaps as a linear range table. The supplementary planes are handled by a single formula (other_ja.c).
